placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_randolph_dearborn, the town's river business front, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its east wall is fixed by the east wall of recon_1835_blk_randolph_dearborn_d6_10, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks at Randolph Street and the river beyond it, as every documented store on this face does. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row facing the river rather than detached cottages set back on grass — and the treatment is what this placement takes from it. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.
placement.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the South Division block bounded by Randolph, State, Washington and Dearborn; standing ON the Randolph Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line river row

frontage.why: T-0105, the succession T-0079 owes: the core density standard applied to the next core block standing below the bar. THE FACE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, by the command T-A14 made of it — tools/measure_street_frontage.py randolph washington market franklin — and on the committed dataset Randolph carries 7 documented records and 7 inferred households against Washington's 1 and 0. Randolph is this block's business face by the town's own record, so the block's one free lot on that face takes the row and both free lots on Washington stay open. THE END RULE IS T-A11'S, READ ON THIS BLOCK: this is the easternmost block the plat module reaches on the Randolph tier, so the town-centre end of its frontage is the WEST one, toward Dearborn Street and the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835 — and the row is graded that way, a storey and a half at the west end, a one-room frame cottage in the middle, and an older log cabin at the east. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the lot's own stretch of it and the end the run packs away from are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. Lot 4 is an interior lot and not a corner one, so the standard's third clause — a corner lot builds to the corner — has nothing to bind here; the run stands off both of its own side lines by that same margin.
